narrative:
On November 21, 2026, the Karnataka High Court achieved an overall hearing rate of 52.3%, hearing 655 out of 1,252 scheduled cases across 36 judges. This represents a noticeable increase in efficiency compared to recent days, rising from 45.1% on November 20 and 23.3% on November 18, even as the total scheduled caseload contracted from 2,632 matters on the previous day.

Judicial performance across courtrooms highlighted significant variations in bench clearance. Justice K. V. Aravind achieved a 100% hearing rate by taking up all 10 scheduled matters, maintaining a perfect clearance performance from November 20. High disposal efficiency was also recorded by Justice S.G. Pandit at 86.7% (26 of 30), Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar at 84.2% (32 of 38), and Justice V Srishananda at 82.1% (55 of 67). Conversely, certain single-judge lists experienced zero progress, most notably Hall 7 under Justice B M Shyam Prasad, where none of the 128 scheduled cases were heard.

Stage-wise conversion showed strong movement in early-stage proceedings. Preliminary hearings converted at 60.7% (150 of 247), orders converted at 57.7% (205 of 355), and admissions reached 55.8% (179 of 321)—both orders and admissions improving upon yesterday's rates of 52.0% and 50.6%, respectively. Final hearing matters continued to see lower throughput, converting at 21.7% (45 of 207). Across subject matters, Writ Petitions (WP) comprised the largest share, with 291 of 584 cases heard (49.8%), marking a rise from 38.6% on the previous day. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) also experienced higher engagement, reaching a 61.6% hearing rate (138 of 224) compared to 45.9% yesterday, while Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) recorded a 42.7% hearing rate across 143 scheduled cases.
